clauses.reason: The sole clause directs that the second sentence of section 1 of EO 12334 be deleted and replaced by a new sentence on the Chairman. That is a self-executing amendment of another order: it was performed on issue, on the order's date 1990-02-14 (the order states no later effective date), and nothing remains for it to command afterwards. The inserted sentence continued inside EO 12334 until EO 12863 of September 13, 1993 (section 3.3) revoked EO 12334 as amended; that later event is recorded as the end of the surviving consequence, not as this order's own end, and it is the formal disposition.

research_rationale:
EO 12701 (February 14, 1990; 55 FR 5953) is a one-paragraph amending order. Its single operative command orders that the second sentence of section 1 of EO 12334 (the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board order of December 4, 1981) be deleted and a new sentence inserted in its place, so that one member is designated by the President as Chairman. The held Federal Register original is read in full: there is no other clause, no duration, no report duty and no delegation. The command is self-executing and was performed when the order issued on 1990-02-14; under the owner's amendment rulings the inserted sentence then lived inside EO 12334 until that order ended. EO 12863 of September 13, 1993 (58 FR 48441, section 3.3) revoked EO 12334 as amended, which ended the surviving sentence. Nothing in the held sources shows any later order, statute or regulation restoring EO 12334 or re-adopting the amended sentence. The recommended provisional status is no.

savings.reason: The only consequence of the order was the replacement sentence about the Chairman inside EO 12334. Section 3.3 of EO 12863 of September 13, 1993 (held as the American Presidency Project transcription of the order; the Federal Register page 58 FR 48441 is also held as a text layer) revokes EO 12334 as amended, so that consequence ended on 1993-09-13 with its parent. No residual right, appointment, transfer or continuing duty arose from EO 12701 itself, and the bounded searches of the U.S. Code, the eCFR and the Office of the Federal Register disposition catalog found no later instrument that revives it.
